headline: MSFT surges on AI efficiency news, Alphabet earnings loom tonight — ASX closes green across the board as US midterms grip global attention.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped last night after news broke it's offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI-driven efficiency reduces headcount needs. Markets loved the cost discipline story — leaner workforce + booming cloud = stronger margins. Earnings are also due imminently, adding excitement.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF had a solid session today, riding the broader enthusiasm around Microsoft's AI efficiency push and continued momentum in the sector. Still down -12.85% overall from your entry, but the daily direction is positive.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a decent day today, up 1.41% at close. No specific news catalyst, but lithium stocks have been bouncing on tentative signs of improving sentiment around EV demand. Still deep in the red overall — this is a stock that needs a sustained lithium price recovery to recover lost ground.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS tracked the strong finish on Wall Street last night — the S&P 500 rose 0.7% and NASDAQ gained 0.82%. Broad US market strength lifted this ETF today on the ASX.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: Steady, unremarkable gain today. DHHF is a globally diversified ETF, so it just quietly ticked up with the general market tone. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up slightly today, consistent with the positive ASX session. A broad diversified fund, it moves gently with the overall market.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged higher today. Emerging markets sentiment remains mixed — Brazil's stocks and currency fell recently on political developments — but the overall ETF held its own on the ASX today.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google's parent dipped about 1% last night ahead of its earnings report, which is due tonight US time. Markets may be trimming positions going in cautiously — and there's a separate headwind with Google's own benchmark showing its Gemini 4 Argon AI model ranks behind Claude and GPT-6 for Android coding tasks, which didn't help sentiment.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two was virtually flat last night — barely any movement. GTA 6 news keeps circulating but there's no fresh catalyst. The stock remains in a holding pattern while the market waits for a release date confirmation.

watch_today.title: Alphabet (GOOG) earnings tonight — big moment
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings tonight US time (after market close in the US, so early Wednesday morning AEST). The stock slipped ~1% last night as traders got cautious ahead of the result. Cloud growth and AI revenue are the key things to watch. There's also the distraction of Google admitting its Gemini 4 Argon AI model lags behind Claude and GPT-6. For a long-term holder, one quarter rarely changes the thesis — but the reaction could be sharp either way.

watch_today.title: Microsoft (MSFT) — strong night, earnings also imminent
watch_today.detail: MSFT jumped +1.54% last night after news it's offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 workers as AI automates more tasks. Markets saw this as a bullish efficiency signal. Microsoft earnings are also due very soon. You're up +20.2% overall on this position — the AI and cloud story remains very much intact. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — small bounce, still down big
watch_today.detail: PLS gained +1.41% today, a welcome move after a brutal stretch. You're still down -57.27% overall on this position. There's no structural news today that changes the lithium oversupply problem. For a long-term holder, this is a patience play — the thesis depends on an eventual lithium price recovery as EV demand grows. No reason to sell into a dip, but no new reason to add either.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF creeping back, still underwater
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF rose +1.11% today, helped by Microsoft's strong session and general AI sector optimism. You're still down -12.85% overall from your entry. The long-term AI investment case is intact — if anything the Microsoft buyout news reinforces how seriously companies are betting on AI productivity. Hold and let it work.

watch_today.title: US midterm elections tomorrow — watch for market volatility
watch_today.detail: The 2026 US midterm elections are essentially upon us (voting day is imminent). Markets typically see some volatility around US election results — especially if congressional control shifts. Your US-exposed holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO, VTS.AX) could see some short-term swings. No action needed — just be prepared for a noisy few days.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision — CPI data in focus this week
watch_today.detail: Australia's CPI (inflation) data is due this week and it's a direct input into whether the RBA raises interest rates. Traders are pricing in a rising chance of another hike. Higher rates would weigh on growth stocks and ETFs like VDHG. Worth keeping an eye on the data when it drops — though for a long-term holder, one rate move doesn't change the game.

world.summary: The dominant global stories today are the looming US midterm elections, escalating tension around a potential US-Iran conflict, China stepping into Middle East diplomacy, and Harry Kane picking up the Ballon d'Or.

stories.title: US midterm elections: Trump pushes voter fraud claims as voting looms
stories.why_it_matters: With the 2026 US midterms just days away, the Trump administration has asked Washington state to set aside hundreds of ballots it suspects were cast by non-citizens — a legally contentious move that legal experts say pushes the boundaries of federal authority over state elections. Trump is also offering cash rewards for anyone who can prove voter fraud. These moves signal a highly contested election cycle and could set up serious post-election disputes if results are close. For Australian investors, a shift in congressional control could affect US fiscal policy, markets, and trade.

stories.title: US and Iran edge closer to direct confrontation
stories.why_it_matters: The New York Times reports a significant escalation in the threat level between the US and Iran, with new intelligence suggesting the risk of a full-blown military confrontation is growing. Mecca pact nations — a group of Muslim-majority countries — are simultaneously holding emergency talks with Iran to try to prevent the Middle East conflict from widening further. A US-Iran war would send oil prices surging and destabilise global markets significantly. Worth watching very closely.

stories.title: China sends envoy to Middle East amid spillover fears
stories.why_it_matters: China has announced it will send a special envoy to the Middle East 'in the near future' as Beijing grows concerned about the conflict spilling over into a broader regional war. This is a notable diplomatic move — China rarely inserts itself this directly into Middle East affairs. It signals how serious the situation has become and suggests even major powers outside the region are alarmed. For Australia, any Middle East escalation affects oil prices (crude is near $101/barrel), which feeds directly into fuel costs and inflation.

stories.title: Netanyahu faces political squeeze — Arab parties could oust him
stories.why_it_matters: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is facing a potentially historic political threat — Arab Israeli parties in the Knesset (Israel's parliament) could combine with the opposition to push him out, if the opposition is willing to break a prior election promise not to work with Arab parties. A Washington Post analysis also notes that even with Trump's backing, Netanyahu could lose an election and still remain in power over a deeply divided Israel. Israeli political instability adds another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile Middle East situation.

stories.title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or after record-breaking season
stories.why_it_matters: England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or — football's most prestigious individual award — following a record-breaking season. This caps a remarkable turnaround for Kane, who left Tottenham without a trophy and has now won the ultimate individual honour. A feel-good moment for football fans globally, and a milestone for English football.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street was a solid night — S&P 500 up 0.7%, NASDAQ up 0.82%, with Microsoft leading the charge. The ASX followed suit today, closing up 0.46% at 8,850. Oil is just under $101/barrel and gold is essentially flat at $4,039. The Aussie dollar is holding just above 70 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed higher today, lifted by the positive lead from Wall Street last night.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid session last night — broad market strength led by tech.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech-heavy index had a good night last night, boosted by Microsoft's AI efficiency story.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Slipped slightly last night but remains elevated above $100. Middle East tensions keeping a floor under prices.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Essentially flat. Gold has been holding at historically high levels amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Holding just above 70 cents. CPI data this week could move it — higher inflation = higher RBA rate odds = stronger AUD.

politics.summary: Domestically, the big stories are a proposed national exams shake-up for schools, the Coalition releasing its budget cut plan ahead of an election, the RBA under fire over government spending, and new drone protection laws for Defence bases.

stories.title: National exams for Years 6, 10 and 12 proposed in major schools overhaul
stories.why_it_matters: A major proposal has been floated to introduce standardised national exams for students in Years 6, 10, and 12 — a significant shake-up to how Australian schools assess students. The idea is to create more consistent benchmarks across states and territories. This would affect millions of families and could reshape how schools prepare students, with critics likely to raise concerns about 'teaching to the test.' No legislation yet, but it's generating serious debate.

stories.title: Coalition releases $31 billion savings plan — cuts to climate, housing and more
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition (opposition) has released a policy platform claiming it would save $31 billion by cutting spending on climate programs, housing initiatives, and other areas. Shadow Treasurer Angus Taylor is framing this as budget discipline ahead of an election. The cuts include pulling back on renewable energy commitments, which is politically contentious given the climate debate. For investors, a change in government would shift energy and housing policy settings significantly.

stories.title: RBA 'hammered' over impact of government spending on inflation
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) is facing criticism over claims that heavy federal government spending is making its job of controlling inflation much harder — effectively forcing the RBA to keep rates higher for longer to offset the stimulus. The RBA Governor has separately issued a 'dire warning' about superannuation being drawn down in ways that could create a spending spiral. This is a slow-burn tension between fiscal policy (what the government spends) and monetary policy (what the RBA does with rates) that directly affects mortgage holders and savers.

stories.title: Australia introduces new laws to protect Defence bases from drones
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has introduced legislation to create drone exclusion zones around Australian Defence Force bases and protect military personnel from drone surveillance or attack. This follows similar moves in the US and UK and reflects growing concern about drones being used for espionage or as weapons near sensitive facilities. It's part of a broader national security tightening as geopolitical tensions rise across the Indo-Pacific.

ai.summary: The big AI stories today: Microsoft is using AI efficiency to justify cutting 60,000 jobs, Google's Gemini AI model is falling behind rivals in coding benchmarks, and the world's top AI labs are joining a UK biosecurity push.

stories.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 staff as AI drives efficiency
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has offered voluntary buyout packages to 60,000 employees — that's roughly 25% of its global workforce — as the company says AI is now doing work that previously required those roles. This isn't a 'struggling company' layoff story; it's a 'we're so good at AI we need fewer people' story. The market loved it, pushing MSFT up 1.54% last night. It's a sign of how quickly AI is reshaping even the largest tech companies from the inside out.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon falls behind Claude and GPT-6 in coding benchmarks
stories.why_it_matters: Google has published its own Android coding benchmark and the results are embarrassing — its newest Gemini 4 Argon AI model ranks well behind both Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-6. Coming from Google itself, this admission is notable. It suggests Google is losing ground in the AI coding assistant race, which is one of the most commercially valuable applications of AI right now. This is part of why GOOG dipped ahead of earnings — investors want to see Google prove it can compete.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind join UK AI Biosecurity Mission
stories.why_it_matters: The UK government has launched a new AI Biosecurity Mission, and all three of the world's leading AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind — have signed on. The initiative is focused on using AI to detect and defend against biological threats, including bioweapons and pandemics. It's a rare moment of collaboration between fierce competitors and signals that governments are taking seriously the dual-use nature of powerful AI (it can help design cures, but also threats). Australia has a stake in this given its close security ties with the UK.

stories.title: Silicon Valley AI groups turn on each other in 2026 midterms
stories.why_it_matters: CNBC reports that AI-focused political groups in Silicon Valley — once broadly aligned — are now openly fighting each other ahead of the US midterms. Some groups are backing AI safety regulations while others are pouring money into anti-regulation candidates. This fracture matters because it shapes the regulatory environment that companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon will operate in. A more regulation-friendly Congress could change the rules of the game for AI investment.

sport.summary: NRL Rugby League World Cup Week 2 is done, the NRL Grand Final result is in (Roosters edged the Knights 19-18), AFL draft talk is heating up, Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or, and Aussie Talia Gibson has a stunning run at the Toray Pan Pacific Open.

stories.title: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in NRL Grand Final thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters have won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in an absolute nail-biter at Accor Stadium. Just one point in it at the final whistle — it doesn't get tighter than that. A huge result for the Roosters faithful and a heartbreaking loss for Newcastle fans.

stories.title: RLWC Week 2: Big crowds and big scorelines
stories.why_it_matters: Week 2 of the Rugby League World Cup delivered big crowds and high-scoring games. The tournament is building serious momentum with strong attendances, suggesting it's capturing public interest globally. No specific scores detailed in the data, but the vibe is overwhelmingly positive for the competition's success.

stories.title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or after record season
stories.why_it_matters: England striker Harry Kane has been awarded the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a record-breaking season. It's the pinnacle of individual achievement in world football and a landmark moment for Kane, who spent years at Tottenham without a major trophy. A massive deal for football fans worldwide.

stories.title: Aussie Talia Gibson stuns Kasatkina 6-0, 7-6 at Toray Pan Pacific Open
stories.why_it_matters: Australian tennis player Talia Gibson pulled off a stunning upset, beating world-class Russian player Daria Kasatkina 6-0, 7-6 in the Round of 32 at the Toray Pan Pacific Open. The dominant first set (6-0) was especially impressive. Gibson now advances to the Round of 16, where she'll face the winner of Alex Eala vs Mika Stojsavljevic. A great result for Australian tennis.

stories.title: AFL: Player names to be mandated on jumpers from next season
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has confirmed that player names will be mandatory on the back of all jumpers from next season — a rule change that seems simple but has been debated for years, with some clubs fiercely protecting their heritage jumper designs. Fans have generally welcomed the move as it makes the game easier to follow. Clubs will need to redesign guernseys accordingly.
